To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the second-order nonlinear optical susceptibility of δ-BiB(3)O(6):Pr(3+) polymer nanocomposites can be enhanced by about 100 times under the illumination of nanosecond laser light pulses.

the second harmonic generation (SHG) of the δ-BiB 3 O 6:Pr(III) nanocomposites can be enhanced up to 10 times in comparison with the pure δ-BiB O 6: Pr(III) crystals, by the photo-illumination of the chalcogenides crystalline substrates with nanosecond laser radiation.
the photo-induced second-harmonic generation in δ-BiB(3)O(6):Pr(3+) nanocomposites deposited onto the AgGaGe(2)Se(6), AgGaGe(3)Se(8), and Ag-Ga-Ga-Ge-3-Se-8:Cu crystalline substrates was studied.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the optimization of the second-order nonlinear optical properties of the nanocomposites based on the δ-BiB 3O 6:Pr 3+ nanoparticles embedded in poly-vinyl alcohol films deposited on the chalco-genside substrates, and the investigation of the underlying mechanisms of the photo-induced effects.

a promising approach to enhance the second harmonic generation efficiency in the δ-BiB(3)O(6):Pr(3+) polymer nanocomposites by means of the photo-induced effects in the AgGaGe(2)Se(6), AgGaGe(0.7)Si(0.3)Se(8), and Ag-Ga- Ge-Se:Cu crystalline substrates.
the development of new nonlinear optical materials for the second-order nonlinear optical processes in nanocomposites.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the photo-induced second-order nonlinear optical effects in the polymer nanocomposites are governed by the photo-excited charge carriers in the chalcogenides, which are responsible for the enhancement of second-order susceptibility in the composites.
the photo-induced SHG effect in the composites was caused by the photo-induced changes in the structure of the chalcogenides.

the photo-induced SHG in the BiB3O6 nanocomposites is a result of the photo-excitation and the following photo-illumination induced structural phase transition from the high-temperature cubic to the low-temperature orthorhombically structured phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the second-order optical nonlinearity can be enhanced by several orders of magnitude by the incorporation of the δ-BiB₆O₃₀:Pr(3+)-PVA composites on the AgGaSe₂ and AgGaGe2-xSizSe₈ (x = 0-0.3) crystals, which are characterized by the large nonlinear susceptibilities and high optical damage thresholds.

the δ-BiB 3O6: Pr(3+) nanocomposites deposited onto chalcogenide substrates can serve for the fabrication of the nonlinear optical devices with the second-order susceptibility enhanced by the orders of magnitude.

the photo-induced enhancement of the SHG in the δ-BiB₄O₇ nanocomposites deposited onto the chalcogenides is a promising approach for the development of novel optical materials for the generation of the second harmonics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photoinduced second-order optical susceptibility enhancement of the polymer nanocomposites can be achieved in the visible spectral range.

the photo-induced enhancement of the second-order nonlinear optical susceptibility in the composites is due to the photo-illumination-induced structural changes of both the crystalline substrate and the δ-BiB(3)O(6) nanoparticles.
the photo-induced second-order nonlinearity in the δ-BiB(3)O(6):Pr(3+) polymer nanocomposite films is strongly influenced by the chemical composition of the crystalline substrates.
